svg.title: Four Checks Before Advertising or Releasing Funds
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-equipment-statutory-risk-preflight; chart type: decision_tree; title: Four Checks Before Advertising or Releasing Funds; subtitle: Each unresolved branch has a specific stop condition and corrective action.; chapter number: 5; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Four ordered decision nodes; numeric values indicate check sequence. Apply the relevant state's enacted UCC and licensing rules. Cornell UCC text is a reference model, not a substitute for identifying the controlling state enactment.; caption: Pass each check with retained evidence. Missing license coverage halts regulated activity; unresolved ownership halts settlement; unsupported condition claims halt publication; unresolved export restrictions halt the affected transaction or shipment.; stages: label: Activity and licensing; value: Proceed only after classifying asset, jurisdiction, and brokerage activity; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Determine whether the activity requires a dealer, vehicle broker, auction, or other state authorization. California Vehicle Code section 11700 is a vehicle dealer example, not a universal CNC licensing rule. If required coverage is absent, stop that activity until the required authorization is effective.; label: Ownership and lien release; value: Proceed only with verified ownership and executable creditor releases; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Apply UCC 9-315 and the applicable title regime. Obtain a payoff statement and asset-specific release or sale authorization from the secured party. Use an authorized UCC-3 amendment or termination under UCC 9-513 as appropriate; do not terminate a broader facility merely because one machine is being sold.; label: Condition and warranties; value: Proceed only with supportable descriptions and explicit contract allocation; numeric value: 3.0; detail: Review seller descriptions, inspection findings, and contract language against applicable UCC 2-312, 2-313, and 2-316. Identify the seller and the broker's authority. Pause unsupported claims; a general as-is statement does not automatically erase an express warranty.; label: Export and payment integrity; value: Proceed only after resolving classification, counterparties, and settlement risks; numeric value: 4.0; detail: For export transactions, determine EAR scope under 15 CFR Part 734, classification and destination controls under Part 738, and restrictions under Parts 744 and 746; also assess applicable OFAC sanctions under 31 CFR Chapter V. Resolve required authorizations before shipment and independently verify escrow and wire instructions before releasing funds.

text.title: Four Checks Before Advertising or Releasing Funds
text.tspan: Four Checks Before Advertising or Releasing Funds

circle.title: label: Activity and licensing; value: Proceed only after classifying asset, jurisdiction, and brokerage activity; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Determine whether the activity requires a dealer, vehicle broker, auction, or other state authorization. California Vehicle Code section 11700 is a vehicle dealer example, not a universal CNC licensing rule. If required coverage is absent, stop that activity until the required authorization is effective.

text.title: Determine whether the activity requires a dealer, vehicle broker, auction, or other state authorization. California Vehicle Code section 11700 is a vehicle dealer example, not a universal CNC licensing rule. If required coverage is absent, stop that activity until the required authorization is effective.

circle.title: label: Ownership and lien release; value: Proceed only with verified ownership and executable creditor releases; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Apply UCC 9-315 and the applicable title regime. Obtain a payoff statement and asset-specific release or sale authorization from the secured party. Use an authorized UCC-3 amendment or termination under UCC 9-513 as appropriate; do not terminate a broader facility merely because one machine is being sold.

text.title: Apply UCC 9-315 and the applicable title regime. Obtain a payoff statement and asset-specific release or sale authorization from the secured party. Use an authorized UCC-3 amendment or termination under UCC 9-513 as appropriate; do not terminate a broader facility merely because one machine is being sold.

circle.title: label: Condition and warranties; value: Proceed only with supportable descriptions and explicit contract allocation; numeric value: 3.0; detail: Review seller descriptions, inspection findings, and contract language against applicable UCC 2-312, 2-313, and 2-316. Identify the seller and the broker's authority. Pause unsupported claims; a general as-is statement does not automatically erase an express warranty.

text.title: Review seller descriptions, inspection findings, and contract language against applicable UCC 2-312, 2-313, and 2-316. Identify the seller and the broker's authority. Pause unsupported claims; a general as-is statement does not automatically erase an express warranty.

circle.title: label: Export and payment integrity; value: Proceed only after resolving classification, counterparties, and settlement risks; numeric value: 4.0; detail: For export transactions, determine EAR scope under 15 CFR Part 734, classification and destination controls under Part 738, and restrictions under Parts 744 and 746; also assess applicable OFAC sanctions under 31 CFR Chapter V. Resolve required authorizations before shipment and independently verify escrow and wire instructions before releasing funds.

text.title: For export transactions, determine EAR scope under 15 CFR Part 734, classification and destination controls under Part 738, and restrictions under Parts 744 and 746; also assess applicable OFAC sanctions under 31 CFR Chapter V. Resolve required authorizations before shipment and independently verify escrow and wire instructions before releasing funds.

Assumptions: Four ordered decision nodes; numeric values indicate check sequence. Apply the relevant state's enacted UCC and licensing rules. Cornell UCC text is a reference model, not a substitute for identifying the controlling state enactment.
